competitors.rationale: Verified on 2026-08-12 (C:FridgeChef). Solves the inventory input problem via fridge photo recognition to suggest recipes, directly addressing ingredient awareness, but lacks weekly meal planning and shopping list workflows.

competitors.pricing_summary: EUR 6.99/month or EUR 49.99/year (converted: EUR 4.17/month on annual plan)
competitors.rationale: Verified on 2026-07-30 (C:MealLoop). Directly targets families with structured weekly meal plans, automated grocery lists, diet filters, and family sharing, though it lacks native fridge and pantry inventory tracking.

Verified on 2024-11-05 (C:PlanPlate). Offers calendar meal planning, shared plans, and recipe importing at an accessible EUR 2.99/month price point, but data is stale (nearly two years old) and it lacks inventory tracking and grocery list generation.

Verified on 2026-06-18 (C:PantryGenie). Directly tracks pantry inventory through barcode scanning, sends expiry alerts, and generates shopping lists, but does not provide end-to-end weekly dinner planning.

competitors.pricing_summary: Free; EUR 29.99 one-off for full recipe pack
competitors.rationale: Verified on 2026-05-02 but lacks a source URL (C:WeekWise). Focuses on budget meal planning and store price comparisons, but lacks inventory integration and verified pricing documentation.

Verified on 2025-01-20 from a homepage rather than a pricing page (C:ZeroWaste Kitchen). Offers leftover use-it-up recipes for eco-conscious cooks, but lacks structured weekly planning, automated shopping lists, and recent verification.

Verified on 2026-08-25 (C:SupperSync). Targets shared households with collaborative meal planning, who-cooks chore rotas, and shared shopping lists at EUR 4.49/month per household, though it does not track pantry or fridge inventory.

white_space: No single competitor unifies existing pantry and fridge inventory awareness (present in C:FridgeChef, C:PantryGenie, C:ZeroWaste Kitchen) with multi-day weekly meal planning and automated shopping lists (present in C:MealLoop, C:PlanPlate, C:SupperSync).

No competitor combines household coordination and shared dinner planning (seen in C:MealLoop, C:PlanPlate, C:SupperSync) with food waste mitigation and inventory tracking (seen in C:PantryGenie, C:ZeroWaste Kitchen).
pricing_anchors: Established market competitors charge between EUR 2.99/month (C:PlanPlate) and EUR 6.99/month (C:MealLoop monthly; EUR 4.17/month when converted from the EUR 49.99 annual plan), with household and inventory apps clustering at EUR 3.99/month (C:PantryGenie) and EUR 4.49/month (C:SupperSync), alongside free ad- or donation-funded options (C:FridgeChef, C:WeekWise, C:ZeroWaste Kitchen). Consumer willingness to pay centers at a median of EUR 3.50 per month for a cooking app (S05). Any subscription price above EUR 4.49/month to EUR 6.99/month is untested and unsupported.

idea_claim_checks.claim: Existing recipe apps give ideas but do not know what you already own.
idea_claim_checks.explanation: Competitor evidence shows multiple apps already capture owned ingredients: C:FridgeChef suggests recipes based on fridge photos, C:PantryGenie tracks pantry items and expiry dates, and C:ZeroWaste Kitchen suggests meals around leftover ingredients. The true differentiation lies in pairing inventory awareness directly with weekly planning, not in inventory awareness alone.

idea_claim_checks.claim: Dinner planning is a daily chore
idea_claim_checks.explanation: Supported by S04, which shows adults spend 22 minutes each day deciding what to cook (noting the study dates from 2023).
Supported by S02, which documents an average weekly grocery expenditure of EUR 118 for a two-person household.

idea_claim_checks.claim: a lot of food gets thrown away
idea_claim_checks.explanation: Supported by S01, which finds that households discard approximately 19% (nearly a fifth) of the food they purchase.
